summary:
Exoworld Explorer is an interactive 3D web application that allows users to explore real exoplanets beyond our Solar System using NASA data. The platform visualizes planetary systems, habitable zones, Earth Similarity Index (ESI), and transit light curves, helping users understand how scientists search for potentially habitable worlds.

Users can select and examine exoplanets such as TRAPPIST-1e, TOI-700d, LHS 1140b, and K2-18b while viewing important characteristics including radius, mass, gravity, orbital period, temperature, and discovery information. The application combines scientific data with immersive 3D visualization to make complex astronomical concepts easier to understand.

The project addresses the challenge of improving access to space science education by transforming real exoplanet datasets into an engaging and interactive learning experience. By allowing users to explore planetary systems visually rather than through raw data, Exoworld Explorer promotes curiosity, scientific literacy, and a deeper understanding of the search for life beyond Earth.
details:
Exoworld Explorer is an interactive 3D web application designed to help users discover and understand exoplanets beyond our Solar System. The platform visualizes real exoplanetary systems using NASA data, allowing users to explore planets orbiting distant stars, view habitable zones, analyze transit light curves, and compare planetary properties with Earth.

Users can select exoplanets such as TOI-700 d, TRAPPIST-1 e, TRAPPIST-1 f, TRAPPIST-1 g, LHS 1140 b, and Kepler-186 f to learn about their radius, mass, gravity, temperature, orbital period, and habitability indicators. The application also calculates and displays the Earth Similarity Index (ESI), helping users understand how closely an exoplanet resembles Earth and whether it may have conditions suitable for life.

The project addresses the challenge of making complex astronomical data more accessible and engaging. Instead of studying exoplanets through large datasets and scientific papers, users can interact with them in a visual environment, making space science easier to understand for students, educators, and astronomy enthusiasts.

Exoworld Explorer was developed using HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Three.js, WebGL, Service Workers, and Progressive Web App (PWA) technologies. NASA Exoplanet Archive and NASA Planetary Fact Sheet data were used to provide reliable planetary and stellar information. The project works both online and offline and can be installed on desktop and mobile devices like a native application.

Our team focused on scientific accuracy, educational value, ease of use, visual clarity, and accessibility while designing the platform. The combination of interactive 3D exploration, habitability analysis, and transit simulation makes Exoworld Explorer a creative tool that transforms real NASA exoplanet data into an immersive learning experience. The intended impact is to inspire curiosity about space exploration, promote STEM education, and help users better understand the search for potentially habitable worlds beyond Earth.
